depiction.subject: Museum map of Sri Lanka during the Anuradhapura period
depiction.event_or_theme: hydraulic, monastic, political and multi-port geography
depiction.period: modern museum representation of c. first millennium BCE–early second millennium CE
depiction.notes: The image documents a national-museum synthesis, not contemporaneous cartography.

vision_review.visual_notes: Island map with hydrography/topography and categorical site symbols. Run45 adds the independently sourced port reading: Mahatittha/Mantai (Mannar), Jambukolapattana, Gokanna/Trincomalee and Godavaya are the major anchors to call out; Uraturai belongs especially to later north/Palk continuity.
vision_review.uncertainty: Fine museum labels remain less reliable than the independent archaeological map and port literature. The period compresses more than a millennium.

tag_review.notes: Run45 deepened the route/port reading and kept the field image as the preferred illustration because rights are user-supplied. Cambridge Antiquity 2018 Figure 1 is retained as a research reference rather than copied as an asset.

human_review.notes: Historical use requires captions to state that this is a museum synthesis.

fragment.caption: La carte du Musée national de Colombo fait apparaître un royaume d’Anuradhapura intérieur mais relié à plusieurs façades maritimes : Mantai/Mahātittha au nord-ouest, Jambukolapaṭṭana au nord, Gokanna/Trincomalee à l’est et Godavaya au sud. Les ports n’ont toutefois ni la même fonction ni la même importance pendant tout le millénaire.
fragment.what_it_shows: A modern spatial synthesis combining water, institutions, settlements and a multi-port maritime system.
fragment.why_here: Makes visible that Anuradhapura's inland hydraulic core was coupled to Indian Ocean exchange through several coastal gateways rather than a single maritime outlet.
fragment.limits: Chronologically compresses a millennium-plus; mapped dots and lines are not simultaneous observations and fine labels should defer to specialist archaeology.

depiction.subject: Museum schematic of ancient Indian Ocean sea routes
depiction.event_or_theme: Indian Ocean connectivity, monsoon circuits and broad maritime technology zones
depiction.period: modern museum synthesis of ancient/early historic maritime exchange
depiction.notes: Solid lines show major sea routes; dashed and x-marked zones are labelled dhow and outrigger technology zones.

vision_review.caption_transcription: TRADE — Ancient Sea Routes; Major Sea Routes; Dhow Technology Zone; Outrigger Technology Zone
vision_review.visual_notes: Sri Lanka lies near intersecting route arcs between western Indian Ocean, India, Bay of Bengal and Southeast Asia. Run45 independently anchors the route logic in scholarship on monsoon seasonality, Mantai and Sri Lanka as an Indian Ocean crossroads.
vision_review.uncertainty: The technology-zone boundaries have no visible date range and are schematic. They must not be rendered as exclusive ethnic/technical frontiers.

tag_review.notes: Use for the geographic proposition `routes + monsoons + port residence`, not as proof of exact dhow/outrigger boundaries.

human_review.notes: Do not caption dhow/outrigger boundaries as precise historical facts without specialist vessel-history sourcing.

fragment.caption: La carte des routes anciennes place Sri Lanka non sur une route unique mais à la couture de circuits saisonniers reliant mer d’Arabie, côtes indiennes, baie du Bengale et Asie du Sud-Est. Les moussons imposaient escales et attentes, un mécanisme qui aide aussi à comprendre l’installation de diasporas marchandes dans les ports.
fragment.what_it_shows: A schematic network of major maritime routes and broad technology zones.
fragment.why_here: Provides a geographic dezoom explaining both Sri Lanka's long-distance connectivity and the formation of resident merchant communities.
fragment.limits: Route curves are schematic; technology zones are chronologically underspecified and should not be read as exclusive borders.
